correctness.rationale: The signature is exp(a e1) exp(b e2) exp(c e1). For each j >= 1, the words 1^i 2^j 1^ell span all degree-(k-j) binary forms after the invertible substitution u=a+c, v=a. The transformed coordinates are exactly the lattice monomials of P_k. The normalized area is k(k-1), and the primitive edge cones yield quotient types 1/(k-1)(1,1) and 1/k(1,k-1); the latter is A_(k-1). Every lattice polygon is normal, so the toric surface is projectively normal.

value.rationale: This is a uniform description for a natural three-segment path family, extending a published order-three example to every k >= 4. It gives the exact lattice polygon, degree, projective normality, and singularity basket, invariants that describe the algebraic complexity and degeneracies of path-signature data. It does not claim to settle the general toricness question.
